⚠️

Take It Seriously

Retatrutide is an investigational medication. This card is about respect for that fact, not hype.

🔍

Understand the potential risks

Investigational means the safety picture is still being studied. I treated that as a reason to be careful, not a reason to rush.

❤️

Health over rapid weight loss

The number on the scale was never the whole goal. Protecting my health while losing weight mattered more than losing it fast.

🌱

Sustainable habits win

Nutrition, recovery, and habits I could actually keep — those did more for me than any shortcut mindset.

Personal experience is not established medical evidence. What happened for me does not predict what happens for anyone else.

🧠

My Mentality

Why I took this seriously

My motivation comes from knowing what it feels like to lose control of my health and how much it affected my everyday life. 💭 The only time I was truly fit was between 2015 and 2017 💪, but after hovering around 200 pounds in 2019, I gained another 30–40 pounds during the pandemic, eventually reaching 240 pounds ⚖️. Being obese wasn't just about how I looked; it meant constant food noise 🍔, overheating while walking around the mall 🥵, painful chafing, acid reflux so severe that I had to change how I slept 😣, and joint pain that made everyday activities miserable.

My gout attacks were especially brutal 🦶, sometimes making even a blanket touching my foot feel like shards of glass, leaving me dependent on crutches just to get around 🩼. I don't want to go back to living that way. 🔥 My mentality is that I have to take my health seriously because I've experienced firsthand what happens when I don't.

I'm sharing my journey because I want to show people that change is possible, that you don't have to accept feeling miserable in your own body, and that sometimes the strongest motivation comes from remembering exactly where you never want to be again. 🎯

💉

My dosing protocol

What I actually did — my personal record, not a protocol to follow.

Personal record only: These are the doses I took, written down as I recorded them. Retatrutide is investigational, and this is not a recommendation, a starting point, or a guide for anyone else. Talk to a qualified healthcare professional before making decisions about medications.
🐢

Start low, build up slowly

Starting low is important — it lets the drug build up in your body gradually. I started at 2.0 mg and stepped up week by week, instead of jumping straight to a high dose.

🎯

The sweet spot, not the highest dose

Getting to a high dose isn't the goal — for me it just meant more weight loss than I needed, and more money spent. My sweet spot was 4 mg to 8 mg weekly, and within that range, 5 mg was where I landed — I held 5 mg for 6–8 weeks. I didn't have to go on a higher dose, because it was my training, diet, and sleep that lost the weight, not a bigger dose.

Tapering off & maintenance

📉

Tapering off

To taper off, I used a 10 mg retatrutide dose, stepping down through the lower doses at the end of the timeline (5.0 → 4.0 → 3.0 → 2.5 mg).

🔄

Maintenance: switch to tirzepatide

If you want maintenance, switch to tirzepatide. My sweet spot there is 1.25 mg weekly — or 2.5 or 5 mg. If you're working up to 5 mg weekly, titrate up there slowly.

There is no established tapering guidance; the lower doses at the end are simply what my record shows.

Build Your Foundation

Five compound lifts, two simple workout days, and cardio you can actually enjoy.

🏋️

Squats

Legs and core. The base of the lower-body days.

💪

Deadlifts

Full-body pulling strength, hips and back.

🛏️

Bench Press

Upper-body pushing strength, chest and arms.

🧗

Pull-Ups

Upper-body pulling strength, back and arms.

⬆️

Overhead Press

Shoulder pressing strength, standing tall.

Workout A

  • Squats
  • Bench Press
3 sets × 10 reps — example starting structure

Workout B

  • Deadlifts
  • Overhead Press
3 sets × 10 reps — example starting structure

Adjust volume and intensity to your own ability. These are examples, not mandatory prescriptions.

🏃 10-minute jog🚶 20-minute walk🏊 30-minute swim

Start at your current fitness level and prioritize proper technique and recovery.

🛡️

Form first, weight second

Proper form is important — especially if you're a beginner, start on a light weight. You want to minimize the risk of injury by focusing on proper technique, and by stretching and warming up before lifting.

🎯

Compound lifts first — and essentials on tired days

Focusing on compound lifts is important: the five lifts above — squats, deadlifts, bench press, pull-ups, overhead press — each work multiple muscle groups at once, which is why they deserve your focus. Isolation work is optional extra. If you feel like doing more, do more. But if you're feeling lazy or tired, just focus on the essentials — and by essentials, I mean the compound lifts above — limited to two compound movements per workout session, so you get in and out of the gym, and call it a win. You can also perform supersets to save time — pair two exercises back-to-back with little rest in between, like combining pull-ups with bicep curls.

Loose skin — built into the plan

Loose skin was part of the plan, not an afterthought: my regimen is built to eliminate it — especially when you combine consistent training with a high-protein diet.

🏃

Cardio

Cardio tones the body by burning fat across your entire frame, which reduces the soft fat layer directly beneath the skin to reveal a leaner shape. Increased blood flow from cardio also delivers oxygen and nutrients to the skin, helping support its natural elastic recovery as fat volume drops.

🏋️

Weight Training

Weight training builds firm muscle underneath, creating structural volume that physically fills out loose skin and shapes your silhouette. By preventing muscle loss during rapid weight reduction, it keeps your skin supported from within rather than hanging over hollowed-out tissue.

🔗

The Combination of Both

Combining cardio and weight training lowers overall body fat while simultaneously building the underlying muscle needed to stretch skin taut and fill in empty space. Together, they maximize fat loss for a leaner frame while ensuring your body has the firm structural base required to minimize sagging skin.

Why these five lifts?

They train the whole body with a small number of movements, which keeps the routine simple enough to repeat week after week. Consistency with a few basics beats a complicated program you quit.

🍽️

Prioritize Protein

Convenient, affordable protein sources that help support muscle while weight comes down.

🍗

Chicken

Versatile, affordable, easy to cook in batches. Costco rotisserie chicken is affordable.

🥚

Eggs

Cheap, quick, and easy to add to any meal. Very easy to eat — and they fill you up without eating much, while still giving you the benefits.

🧈

Tofu

Budget-friendly plant protein that takes on any flavour. You can look up dishes online — something simple is tofu in chili oil with rice.

🐟

Fish

Lean protein with a different flavour profile for variety. Fish is also a source of omega-3 fatty acids, vitamin D, and selenium — nutrients that support overall health as part of a balanced diet. On cost, canned options like tuna and sardines, and frozen fillets, keep it affordable.

🥩

Steak

Choose lean cuts like eye of round, and use a meat tenderizer — it breaks down the tough fibers in lean cuts so they come out tender. Leaner cuts are not as tasty as fatty cuts, but when you strike a fatty spot, it's much more satisfying than eating a steak that's already fatty.

🐖

Pork

Another everyday protein that keeps meals from getting boring. Lean cuts like pork loin and tenderloin are high in protein and provide B vitamins — especially thiamine — plus zinc and selenium. And pork is often cheaper per pound than beef, which makes it a budget-friendly staple.

🍞

Carbs aren't the enemy — here's the science, simply

Eating carbs 🍞 can still help you lose weight, because weight loss comes down to eating less energy than you burn 🔥, not to banning one food group 🚫 — and carbs fuel your workouts 🏋️, which is part of how the weight comes off. Here's what happens inside: your body stores spare carbs as glycogen 📦, tucked away in your muscles 💪 and liver, and it burns that stored glycogen first 🔥 when it needs quick energy. When you eat fewer carbs, those glycogen stores run low 📉 — and once they're depleted, your body has to find fuel somewhere else, so it starts tapping into fat storage. That's why lower-carb stretches can mean more fat loss 📉. One honest note: part of the fast early drop on low carbs is water 💧, because glycogen holds water with it — but once stores are low, more of the loss comes from fat.

🔇

Food noise, muted

Retatrutide muted food noise for me, so when I was hungry, making food choices felt easy. And the choice was simple: when you're hungry, reach for high protein.

🥚

Every day in my first month

Something I ate every day in my first month on Retatrutide: 3 large eggs, boiled, dipped in salt and pepper. Simple, cheap, filling — my daily staple.

Hydration & Electrolytes

The fundamentals first. Most supplements are optional, not the starting point.

💧

Water

Hydration is essential when using GLP-1 medications like tirzepatide or investigational retatrutide, as reduced appetite and gastrointestinal symptoms can make it easier to become dehydrated. Water supports digestion, regular bowel movements, and exercise performance. 💦 Water-rich foods like watermelon 🍉, Chinese pear 🍐, and strawberries 🍓 also contribute to daily hydration. 🌿 Spring water vs. distilled water: Spring water naturally contains varying amounts of minerals like calcium and magnesium, while distilled water has most minerals removed. Distilled water does not flush electrolytes out faster, but spring water can contribute small amounts of minerals. Ultimately, both hydrate effectively, so prioritize consistent fluid intake and replace electrolytes when significant losses occur through sweating, vomiting, or diarrhea.

🥤

Electrolyte powders

Electrolytes help regulate fluid balance, nerve signaling, and muscle function, making them especially relevant when you're exercising, sweating heavily, or eating substantially less than usual. ⚡ A suitable electrolyte powder can help replace sodium and other electrolytes lost through sweat, while oral rehydration solutions can be particularly useful during fluid losses from vomiting or diarrhea. Choose a formulation appropriate for your activity level and dietary needs, and remember that electrolytes complement adequate nutrition and hydration rather than replacing meals. 💪

🧂

Salt — Celtic Sea Salt

Sodium is an essential electrolyte that helps regulate fluid balance, nerve signaling, and muscle contractions. ⚡ When using GLP-1–based medications such as tirzepatide, or investigational retatrutide, reduced appetite can mean eating less food and consequently getting less sodium from your diet. Celtic sea salt is a popular option because it is minimally refined and retains trace minerals naturally present in the salt, although the amounts of minerals such as magnesium and potassium are small and shouldn't be relied on as a significant source of electrolytes. 🌿 Getting enough sodium through a balanced diet helps support normal hydration, particularly when you're exercising or sweating heavily. Rather than automatically adding salt to every glass of water, adjust your intake to your diet, activity level, and individual needs, especially if you have high blood pressure or kidney or heart conditions. 💧

🫘

Magnesium

Magnesium supports muscle and nerve function, energy metabolism, and normal muscle contraction and relaxation. 🔋 During significant weight loss, eating smaller portions can make it more challenging to obtain sufficient magnesium if your diet lacks foods such as nuts, seeds, leafy greens, legumes, and whole grains. Prioritizing magnesium-rich foods helps support recovery and overall nutritional health, while supplementation may be useful when dietary intake is insufficient. 🌿 Some forms of magnesium can cause diarrhea, so the type and amount matter, especially if gastrointestinal symptoms occur during treatment. Magnesium malate: 200–300 mg daily. Unlike magnesium glycinate, which can make you drowsy and is better left for nighttime, malate doesn't do that.

🍌

Potassium

Potassium is essential for fluid balance, nerve transmission, and normal muscle function, including the muscles involved in your heartbeat. 🍌 When appetite is suppressed and food intake decreases, maintaining a diet containing potassium-rich foods—such as avocados 🥑, leafy greens 🥬, beans, and potatoes—becomes particularly important. Adequate potassium intake supports normal physiological function and complements sodium in maintaining fluid balance. Supplementation should be individualized because excessive potassium can be dangerous, particularly for people with kidney disease or those taking certain medications. Potassium citrate: 200–400 mg daily.

Safety note: Electrolyte needs vary. Excess potassium can be dangerous, especially with kidney problems or certain medications.
💊

The Supplement Shelf

🐟

Fish oil

Fish oil provides omega-3 fatty acids, particularly EPA and DHA, which support heart health and normal cellular function. When using GLP-1 medications such as tirzepatide or investigational retatrutide, reduced appetite can mean eating less fish and getting fewer omega-3s from food. 🧠 Fish oil can help supplement your intake when fatty fish like salmon 🐟 isn't regularly part of your diet. Taking it with a meal may improve tolerance, although some people experience fishy burps or mild stomach discomfort.

☀️

Vitamin D3

Vitamin D3 supports bone health, calcium absorption, muscle function, and immune health. When appetite decreases during GLP-1 treatment, smaller portions and less varied meals can make it harder to obtain sufficient vitamin D from food. 🌞 Sunlight contributes to vitamin D production, but factors such as season, skin exposure, and time outdoors affect how much your body makes. Taking D3 with a meal containing some fat can improve absorption, particularly if your dietary intake or vitamin D levels are low.

🌿

Methylfolate

Methylfolate is a form of vitamin B9 involved in DNA synthesis, cell growth, and red blood cell formation. During GLP-1–assisted weight loss, reduced food intake can make it more difficult to consistently obtain folate from leafy greens 🥬, legumes, and other nutrient-rich foods. Methylfolate supplements may help address inadequate intake when supplementation is appropriate, supporting normal cellular function while you lose weight. A varied diet remains important, and folate supplementation is most useful when it addresses a genuine dietary gap or identified need.

💉

Vitamin B12 — Methylcobalamin

Vitamin B12 supports nerve function, red blood cell production, and normal energy metabolism. When GLP-1 medications suppress appetite, eating smaller portions of meat, eggs, dairy, and other B12-containing foods may reduce your intake. 🍳 Methylcobalamin is one form of B12 that can help meet your needs when dietary intake is insufficient or a deficiency is present. Maintaining adequate B12 is especially important during prolonged weight loss because deficiency can contribute to fatigue, weakness, and neurological symptoms.

🫙

Cod liver oil

Cod liver oil provides omega-3 fatty acids alongside vitamins A and D, making it a convenient way to obtain several nutrients in one supplement. 🐟 During GLP-1–assisted weight loss, when smaller meals can reduce your intake of essential nutrients, it may help supplement a diet that contains little oily fish. The combination can support omega-3 intake and help meet vitamin D needs when dietary intake is insufficient. ☀️ Check the amounts of vitamins A and D on the label, especially if you also take a multivitamin or separate supplements, to avoid excessive intake.

💊

Multivitamin

A multivitamin can help fill nutritional gaps when GLP-1 medications reduce appetite and make it harder to eat a varied, balanced diet. 🥗 By providing a range of vitamins and minerals, it can support normal energy metabolism, immune function, and other essential bodily processes during weight loss. Think of it as nutritional backup for days when your meals are smaller or less varied, rather than a replacement for protein-rich foods, vegetables, fruits, and healthy fats. Check the label for overlapping nutrients—particularly vitamins A and D—if you're also taking cod liver oil or individual supplements.

Watch the overlap: cod liver oil contains vitamins A and D, so combining it with other supplements can lead to excessive intake.

Supplements should reflect individual nutritional needs. No dosages are given here and no specific health outcomes are promised.

🌙

Sleep & Recovery

Wind the day down, then sleep deep

Aim for 7–9 hours of sleep nightly for adults. Get natural daylight during the day, take walks outdoors when practical, and keep a consistent sleep schedule.

Two light habits do a lot of the work: 10 minutes of direct sunlight, and a walk to watch the sunset. Your body's internal clock — your circadian rhythm — takes its cues from light. Bright light during the day signals it to stay alert, and the fading light of sunset signals it to wind down and get ready for sleep. Morning sun and a sunset walk bookend the day and tell your body when to be awake and when to sleep.

☀️ Daylight→🚶 Daily movement→🌇 Sunset walk→🌆 Evening wind-down→😴 Sleep

Recovery is what lets training actually work. Without sleep, everything else gets harder.

After Weight Loss: Areas to Research

⚖️ 1. Weight loss & maintenance — Retatrutide or Tirzepatide

After reaching your target weight, the next step is maintaining your results while keeping appetite and cravings manageable. 🎯 Many people in online weight-loss communities share positive experiences with tirzepatide, describing quieter food noise, better portion control, fewer cravings, and feeling more in control of their eating habits. 🧬 Retatrutide has also generated significant interest for its effects on body weight and metabolic pathways, making it a prominent topic in discussions about next-generation weight-management treatments. The focus after weight loss is to maintain your progress, build sustainable habits, and preserve the muscle you've worked hard to develop. 💪

💪 2. Muscle growth & body composition — CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin or Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin

After losing significant weight, you can shift your focus toward building a stronger, leaner, and more defined physique. 🏋️ CJC-1295 and ipamorelin are discussed in peptide communities for their relationship with growth-hormone signaling, while tesamorelin is known for its effects on abdominal fat in its approved medical application. 🧬 Online discussions frequently highlight interest in improved body composition, sleep, and training recovery when exploring these compounds. Combined with progressive resistance training, adequate protein 🍗, and consistent sleep 😴, this phase is about developing strength, supporting lean mass, and continuing to improve your physique.

🩹 3. Recovery & tissue health — BPC-157 + TB-500

As you become stronger and increase your training volume, recovery becomes an important part of maintaining consistency and progressing toward your goals. 🏃 BPC-157 and TB-500 have attracted considerable attention in peptide communities, where users share experiences involving mobility, exercise recovery, and improvements in how their bodies feel after training. 🔬 Their connection to experimental research on tissue repair and healing mechanisms has made them popular topics among people interested in recovery science. Prioritizing sleep 😴, nutrition 🥗, sensible training progression, and recovery practices helps support your ability to stay active and work toward your fitness goals.

✨ 4. Skin health & appearance — GHK-Cu, GLOW or KLOW

After significant weight loss, skin quality and appearance can become an important part of completing your overall transformation. ✨ GHK-Cu has attracted attention for its relationship with collagen-associated processes and skin research, while GLOW and KLOW are discussed in peptide communities as blends intended to combine multiple compounds for skin-focused goals. 🧬 Online skincare discussions often highlight interest in smoother-looking skin, improved texture, and a more refreshed appearance when exploring copper peptides and related products. Combined with consistent skincare 🧴, sun protection ☀️, and good nutrition, skin health can become another focus as you work toward your desired post-weight-loss appearance.

The Bottom Line

Everything above, in one place.

  • 🧠 Mentality — Take your health seriously, because you've seen what happens when you don't — and never go back to living that way.
  • 💉 Protocol — Start low and build up gradually. My sweet spot was 5 mg held 6–8 weeks, not the highest dose. Taper off on a 10 mg retatrutide dose; for maintenance, switch to tirzepatide, sweet spot 1.25 mg weekly (or 2.5 or 5).
  • 🏋️ Training — Compound lifts first, two per session, form before weight. Do more if you feel like it; on tired days, just hit the essentials and get out. Supersets save time. Cardio, weights, and high protein also work against loose skin.
  • 🥗 Nutrition — Protein first, affordable foods, and carbs aren't the enemy: when glycogen runs low, the body taps fat storage. With food noise muted, hungry choices feel easy.
  • 💧 Hydration — Water sipped through the day, since retatrutide suppresses thirst. Electrolytes for workouts and heavy sweat, plus Celtic sea salt adjusted to diet and activity.
  • 💊 Supplements — Fish oil, D3, methylfolate, and B12 — plus cod liver oil and a multivitamin, checking for A and D overlap.
  • 😴 Sleep — 7–9 hours, with morning sunlight and a sunset walk setting the clock.
  • 🌱 Beginner — You don't need six days a week: resistance 2–3 days, cardio 2–3 days, protein, water, and sleep. Manageable habits, kept over time.
  • 📊 Results — Weight 240.4 → 178.0 lbs (−62.4 lbs).
  • 🔬 Research Areas — An educational overview, not a protocol: weight loss & maintenance, muscle & body composition, recovery & tissue health, skin & appearance.

The goal isn't just to weigh less. It's to build healthier habits you can maintain over time.
